stories.summary: Sudan: UN Report Details Deadly Civilian Impact of Surge in Drone Strikes 17 November 2026 United Nations in Sudan (Khartoum) press release Persistent disregard for the protection of civilians has continued to exact "an unbearable toll" on the Sudanese people, a report published today by the UN Human Rights Office finds. The report, which covers the first half of 2026, documents trends and patterns that have been consistent throughout the conflict, including the targeting of civilians and civilian objects, indiscriminate attacks, reprisals against civilians accused of "collaboration" with opposing forces, and the continued use of sexual violence as a weapon of war. It also raises concerns about continued unlawful killings, arbitrary detention, and erosion of civic space. At least 1,390 civilians were killed in the conflict between the Sudanese Armed Forces, the Rapid Support Forces and allied armed movements between January and June this year. More than 80 per cent of these casualties were the result of drone strikes -- which have come to be a "defining feature" of the war, says the report.

stories.summary: Liberia Lifts a Major Barrier to Education Pixabay 16 November 2026 Human Rights Watch (Washington, DC) By Jo Becker Families Report Benefits from New Ban on School Registration Fees "Our children are able to go to school again." Since the policy took effect in September, Liberian child advocates have interviewed parents in four counties to assess whether schools were complying with the ban. The findings offered encouraging early indications: nearly all 20 parents interviewed knew about the policy and had enrolled their children without paying registration fees. The pilot project is expected to start on a small scale, with perhaps 100 or 200 deportees.

A plan to set up so-called return hubs in a non-EU country had been announced by the group — which also includes Austria, the Netherlands, Greece and Denmark — back in September . Monday's announcement comes after the EU introduced new regulations to speed up deportations and allow the establishment of hubs outside of the bloc. EU policymakers have shifted focus toward improving their broken repatriation system, which currently sees less than 30 percent of people ordered to leave the bloc returned to their country of origin. Speaking after Monday's meeting in Vienna, Austrian Chancellor Christian Stocker, who called the decision "a truly historic paradigm shift in migration policy," summed up the plan by saying, "If returning [migrants] to their home country is not possible, then in the future people without a right of residence will be sent back to a third country such as Rwanda." Danish Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen lauded the project as a "milestone" that will send a "signal... that you can no longer enter the European Union illegally and think that you can just stay around." Ces derniers, notamment nécessaires à la transition énergétique, au numérique ou encore à la Défense sont extrêmement convoités et se retrouvent en première ligne des intérêts géostratégiques. En premier lieu, le rapport documente donc des réseaux de prédation internes aux États. « Le Tchad , sur le terrain des minerais critiques, produit de l'antimoine.

stories.title: Éliminatoires CAN 2027: Côte d'Ivoire, RDC, Cameroun, Sénégal... Qui peut se qualifier lors de la 4e journée?
stories.summary: Éliminatoires CAN 2027: Côte d'Ivoire, RDC, Cameroun, Sénégal... Qui peut se qualifier lors de la 4e journée? La 4e journée des éliminatoires de la CAN 2027 s'étale sur les journées de lundi 16 et mardi 17 novembre. Cameroun, Sénégal, Côte d'Ivoire, Maroc, RDC... Plusieurs grosses nations africaines auront déjà la possibilité de se qualifier pour le grand rendez-vous continental en cas de résultat favorable.

stories.title: Élections au Cameroun : au sein du parti de Paul Biya, les jeunes loups à l’assaut de la vieille garde
stories.summary: À l’approche des élections locales au Cameroun, de jeunes militants du RDPC défient les barons établis du parti présidentiel. Une guerre générationnelle inédite, qui met les figures historiques du parti de Paul Biya sous forte pression.

stories.title: Menace jihadiste en Guinée: «Il y a un déficit de maillage sécuritaire du gouvernement guinéen»
stories.summary: Le grand invité Afrique Menace jihadiste en Guinée: «Il y a un déficit de maillage sécuritaire du gouvernement guinéen» Publié le : 16/11/2026 - 06:51 Le jihadisme « aux portes de la Guinée », c'est le titre d'une étude publiée récemment par la Fondation Konrad-Adenauer. Le rapport montre comment le Jnim, lié à al-Qaïda et très actif au Mali, s'est installé autour de la frontière avec la Guinée pour en faire une base arrière. Le groupe terroriste s'appuie sur des relais locaux pour assurer son implantation dans la région de la Haute-Guinée, en utilisant le pastoralisme et l'orpaillage (deux activités multiséculaires des populations des deux côtés de la frontière). Un nouveau front jihadiste ouest-africain peut-il émerger en Guinée ? Aliou Barry, qui dirige le Centre d'analyse et d'études stratégiques, répond aux questions de Sidy Yansané.

stories.title: Africa: Reaching Isolated Areas Crucial To Stopping Ebola
stories.summary: Six Months On, Accessing Hard-to-Reach Communities Key to Halting Ebola Outbreak 15 November 2026 Content from a Premium Partner Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention (Addis Ababa) Six months into the Ebola outbreak caused by Bundibugyo virus in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, significant progress has been made in bringing lifesaving services closer to affected communities, despite immense challenges. However, fuelled by ongoing conflict, displacement and humanitarian needs, the outbreak continues to expand, particularly in affected areas. Since the start of the outbreak, more than 11 000 cases and 5400 deaths have been reported. Children account for more than a quarter of confirmed cases and one third of deaths. Seven in 10 children under five with confirmed Ebola have died.

stories.title: L'Algérie accuse le Maroc d'être à l'origine de la pollution d'un cours d'eau
stories.summary: L'Algérie accuse le Maroc d'être à l'origine de la pollution d'un cours d'eau Le gouvernement algérien accuse le Maroc de polluer délibérément un cours d'eau qui alimente un barrage. L'incident a même été porté jusqu'à la tribune de la COP31 en Turquie. Rabat de son côté a voulu temporiser alors que certains parlementaires algériens exigent des sanctions contre cette pratique qui est vue en Algérie comme une menace environnementale. Publié le : 16/11/2026 - 05:52 Modifié le : 16/11/2026 - 05:52 1 min Temps de lecture Des drapeaux algériens et marocains dans la ville d'Oujda, frontière franco-marocaine. © FADEL SENNA / AFP Par : RFI Publicité Lire la suite C'est un nouvel épisode qui alimente la brouille entre le Maroc et l' Algérie . La situation au niveau du barrage de Hammam Boughrara, situé à l'extrême ouest de la wilaya de Tlemcen, tout près de la frontière avec le Maroc, laisse craindre une « véritable catastrophe environnementale » généralisée, a déclaré la semaine dernière Karim Arab, directeur général de l'Observatoire national de l'environnement et du développement durable.

stories.title: Patrimoine mondial: la Chine propose à l'Afrique de l'aider à classer ses sites sur la liste de l'Unesco
stories.summary: Patrimoine mondial: la Chine propose à l'Afrique de l'aider à classer ses sites sur la liste de l'Unesco Alors que moins de 10 % des sites actuellement inscrits sur la liste du patrimoine mondial de l'Unesco se trouvent en Afrique, Pékin offre aux pays du continent de les accompagner et de financer les candidatures des biens qu'ils entendent déposer auprès de l'organisation. Un investissement dans la mémoire africaine non dénué d'arrière-pensées... Publié le : 16/11/2026 - 05:03 Modifié le : 16/11/2026 - 05:04 2 min Temps de lecture En 2023, la Chine a aidé le Bénin à étendre à son territoire le classement du paysage du Koutammakou dont la partie togolaise figurait déjà sur la liste du patrimoine mondial de l'Unesco. © Getty Images/Godong/robertharding Par : RFI Publicité Lire la suite Avec notre correspondante à Pékin, Clea Broadhurst La Chine veut remédier à la sous-représentation des sites africains inscrits au patrimoine mondial de l' Unesco . Alors que moins de 10 % de ceux qui figurent sur la fameuse liste de l'organisation onusienne se trouvent sur le continent, Pékin propose d’accompagner et de financer les candidatures africaines à travers une coopération qui a déjà porté ses fruits par le passé. Au mois d'octobre dernier, une vingtaine de responsables du patrimoine issus de 17 pays africains ont ainsi participé à une formation spécialisée dans le sud-est de la Chine.

stories.title: Town rebuilt after devastating floods becomes showcase for Libyan strongman's rule
stories.summary: Image source, AFP via Getty Images Image caption, Whole areas of Derna have been entirely rebuilt By Tim Whewell Reporting from Derna Published 16 November 2026 "It was joy when I moved in. I could finally relax," says Abdulwahab Damdoum, surveying his luxurious new apartment overlooking the Mediterranean Sea, in the eastern Libyan city of Derna. Just three years ago he was clinging in terror to the roof of a house as the world's deadliest flood this century surged around him. Now the 27-year-old port worker, his wife and two young daughters have been given a new, free, 300-sq-m home in a showcase development commissioned by a son of Khalifa Haftar, the warlord who controls eastern Libya. It is part of a rapid $2bn (Â£1.5bn) rebuilding of Derna that the powerful Haftar family hope will serve as a model for development throughout Libya, increasing their influence across a country currently split between east and west, with rival governments in charge.

stories.title: Les Émirats arabes unis, plaque tournante de l'or exporté illégalement d'Afrique
stories.summary: Chronique des matières premières Les Émirats arabes unis, plaque tournante de l'or exporté illégalement d'Afrique Publié le : 16/11/2026 - 00:27 C'est une étude qui montre l'ampleur de la contrebande de l'or africain. Plus de 450 tonnes d'or sorties illégalement des pays producteurs ont transité par les Émirats arabes unis en 2024, révèle l'enquête de l'ONG Swissaid. Un négociant en or émirati tient des lingots d'or dans une boutique du Souk de l'Or de Dubaï, le 13 avril 2026. AFP - FADEL SENNA Publicité Ce chiffre est un minimum, puisqu'il ne porte que sur l'or qui a transité par les Émirats arabes unis : les volumes exportés sans être déclarés dans les pays où ils sont extraits sont peut-être plus élevés. Il n'en est pas moins un très bon indicateur, car les Émirats sont devenus une plaque tournante incontournable du raffinage de l'or pour toute la filière africaine, qu'elle soit légale ou illégale. « Tous les pays africains qui pèsent dans le secteur sont liés à Dubaï et aux autres émirats », pointe le rapport de Swissaid .

stories.title: Au Ghana, la difficile réinstallation des rapatriés d'Afrique du Sud
stories.summary: Reportage Afrique Au Ghana, la difficile réinstallation des rapatriés d'Afrique du Sud Publié le : 16/11/2026 - 00:07 Que deviennent les ressortissants ghanéens évacués d'Afrique du Sud ? Les autorités ghanéennes ont rapatrié près de 2 000 personnes après les attaques et intimidations xénophobes en Afrique du Sud. Alors que l'opposition conteste la transparence des dépenses engagées pour cette opération, une autre question se pose : celle de la réinstallation. L'enseignant Niinii Armah Armarh est l'un de ces rapatriés. Depuis, il tente de reprendre sa vie à Accra.

stories.title: En Côte d’Ivoire, ces fidèles sur lesquels s’appuie Patrick Achi
stories.summary: En Côte d’Ivoire, ces fidèles sur lesquels s’appuie Patrick Achi Compagnons de longue date, alliés politiques et relais à l’international : le président de l’Assemblée nationale ivoirienne peut compter sur un réseau de proches constitué au fil de son parcours au sommet de l’État. Tour d’horizon de ceux qui forment aujourd’hui sa garde rapprochée. Ses plus proches collaborateurs Ses relais sur le terrain Ses alliés politiques Son réseau international Par Florence Richard Publié aujourd'hui à 12h05 Lecture : 1 minute. Depuis son éviction de la primature, en octobre 2023, au profit de Robert Beugré Mambé , l’ancien chef du gouvernement s’était fait plus discret.

stories.title: Djibouti : comment l’hôpital Al-Shifa veut s’imposer en hub médical sous-régional
stories.summary: Avec l’ouverture du nouvel hôpital Al-Shifa, Djibouti entend moderniser son offre de soins et limiter les évacuations sanitaires à l’étranger. Un projet public confié au privé pour devenir un pôle médical régional.

stories.title: OIF : huis clos sous haute tension et vif échange entre Kagame et Macron
stories.summary: La bataille pour le secrétariat général de l’OIF a provoqué de vives tensions lors du sommet de la Francophonie, à Phnom Penh. Selon nos informations, les présidents français et rwandais ont eu une explication particulièrement houleuse. Malgré les pressions françaises, Kigali maintient la candidature de Louise Mushikiwabo.

stories.title: Brouillé avec Donald Trump, Cyril Ramaphosa en visite aux États-Unis pour tenter de séduire les géants de la tech
stories.summary: En plein froid diplomatique avec les États-Unis, le président sud-africain met le cap sur la Silicon Valley pour attirer des investissements dans le secteur de l’intelligence artificielle. Aucun passage par Washington n’est prévu.

stories.title: ‘Like many men of his generation, he tends to push his feelings down from his heart to his toes’: Meera Sodha on her father’s homecoming
stories.summary: Meera Sodha and her father Raj in Adjumani District, northern Uganda. stories.title: Ebola en RDC : 5 471 décès pour 11 197 cas cumulés ont été recensés en six mois
stories.summary: En RD Congo, six mois que sévit l’épidémie d’Ebola. Déclarée officiellement le 15 mai dernier, cette 17e épidémie est devenue, en quelques mois, la plus meurtrière de l’histoire du pays, qui compte plus de 100 millions d’habitants. Selon le dernier bilan des autorités sanitaires, 5 471 décès pour 11 197 cas cumulés ont été recensés.

stories.title: My mother told me I would die if I sought treatment for Ebola - I am proof you can survive
stories.summary: Image source, Braton Serge/BBC By Ruth Alonga BBC Africa ,Â Reporting from Butembo Published 15 November 2026 When Dr Raymond Kasereka Kamwanga told his family he suspected he had Ebola and was going to a treatment centre in the city of Butembo in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo, his family were horrified. They regarded the specialised unit as a "death house" as not many patients do recover - especially those admitted in the late stages of the illness. His 50-year-old mother was in tears, pleading with him not to go there. "Why are you choosing to die at the Ebola treatment centre?" Masika Ndungo had asked him. But as a doctor at Butembo's Katwa Hospital, he knew that if stayed at home, he was unlikely to survive. This was in July, two months after the World Health Organization (WHO) had declared the Ebola outbreak in DR Congo a public health emergency of international concern.

stories.title: Enseignement supérieur en Afrique : l'UM6P, un modèle d'excellence à suivre ?
stories.summary: L'Afrique peut-elle former ses propres élites sans les envoyer étudier à l'étranger ? Au Maroc, l'Université Mohammed VI Polytechnique (UM6P) s'impose parmi les établissements africains les mieux classés à l'international. Recherche, intelligence artificielle, robotique, agriculture : l'université mise sur des formations de pointe pour répondre aux défis du continent. Mais cette excellence est-elle accessible à tous ? Et ce modèle peut-il être reproduit ailleurs en Afrique ?

stories.title: Présidence de la Francophonie : Louise Mushikiwabo "candidate jusqu'au bout"
stories.summary: C’est une information révélée par nos confrères de Jeune Afrique : la France aurait demandé au Rwanda de retirer sa candidature pour le poste de secrétaire général de l’Organisation internationale de la Francophonie. stories.title: Nigeria's upcoming election marred by rising AI disinformation
stories.summary: https://p.dw.com/p/5PRq5 Prefer DW on Google Nigeria's 2027 general election will take place against the backdrop of AI-driven disinformation Image: Adekunle Ajayi/NurPhoto/picture alliance Advertisement Nigeria has just over two months to go until its general election, with incumbent Bola Tinubu running on a ticket focused on combating raging insecurity and resolving the nation's economic crisis . He faces off against former Vice President Atiku Abubakar and senior opposition figure Peter Obi. The country's electoral body, the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC), recently released its preliminary voter's register, which reportedly is riddled with images believed to have been generated using artificial intelligence (AI) . Among the telltale signs of AI usage were exaggerated facial features in images and inconsistencies on the electoral registers, such as duplicates of names and even identities of people who since the previous election had died. The development raises concerns about the body's overall preparedness ahead of the country's upcoming 2027 general election.

stories.title: South Sudan’s National Election, Its First, Will Be Delayed
stories.summary: Advertisement SKIP ADVERTISEMENT Officials in South Sudan, the world’s youngest state, said on Saturday that its first national election would be postponed, raising new questions about a vote that analysts had already said could not yield a credible result. The National Elections Commission said in a statement that the presidential and legislative elections, which had been scheduled for Dec. 22, would be held on Feb. 11 instead. The country’s information minister, Ateny Wek Ateny, said the postponement would allow more time to register voters and educate them about the process. South Sudan has never held a national election. Since gaining independence from Sudan in 2011 after decades of war, it has been ruled by President Salva Kiir, and it has faced seemingly intractable political difficulties.

stories.title: Russie-Afrique : une stratégie d’influence entravée par les retombées de la guerre en Ukraine
stories.summary: Russie-Afrique : une stratégie d’influence entravée par les retombées de la guerre en Ukraine Un document confidentiel dévoile la feuille de route de la diplomatie russe en Afrique pour les trois prochaines années. stories.summary: La décision, début novembre, des autorités guinéennes d’interdire l'orpaillage "anarchique" dans la région de Siguiri, a provoqué le départ de dizaines de milliers d’orpailleurs, en grande partie vers le Mali, et fait éclater des violences le 11 novembre. stories.title: Présidentielle au Cap-Vert : derrière la stabilité politique, des défis sociaux à relever
stories.summary: Les électeurs du Cap-Vert sont appelés aux urnes, dimanche, pour élire leur président. Considéré comme un îlot de stabilité, cet archipel d'Afrique de l'Ouest connaît une croissance dynamique mais peine à endiguer l'exode de sa jeunesse.

stories.title: Terror from the skies: drones are redefining warfare in Sudan, and massacring its civilians
stories.summary: View image in fullscreen Terror from the skies: drones are redefining warfare in Sudan, and massacring its civilians Composite: Guardian Design / Getty Images Strikes with huge death tolls are an increasing occurrence as UAVs ‘bring the war to places that were once safe’ The first drone struck the busy transport hub near a market in Al-Dibab as hundreds of people gathered to board trucks to take them back to their homes. Ten minutes later on the evening of 18 October, a second drone hit the same site in the town in West Kordofan state, Sudan . At least 139 people were killed. Eight days after the “double-tap” attack – designed to maximise casualties by killing and injuring emergency responders, volunteers and bystanders on top of the original victims – a drone hit a busy market in Nyala, the capital of South Darfur. Emergency Lawyers, a rights group tracking violence in Sudan, put the death toll from that attack at 103. “I lost my 19-year-old son,” a Nyala resident told Agence France-Presse. “We buried him alongside more than 70 bodies in a single site.” View image in fullscreen The remains of Alneam market after a drone strike in the disputed Abyei region along the border between South Sudan and Sudan last month.

stories.title: Jojo the gorilla has spent his life alone. Can he finally find a companion?
stories.summary: By Victoria Gill Science correspondent In 2015, a young male gorilla named Jojo took his first tentative steps onto grass. Until that moment, the 11-year-old ape had spent almost his entire life in a tiny cage at a private zoo in Gabon, after being taken from the wild as an infant. His family had been killed by the poachers who took him. More than a decade later, Jojo is settled into a sanctuary â but he still lives alone. He hasn't had a family since he was taken, or indeed any gorilla friends.

stories.title: Arrested generals and a threatened VP: President's son fuels Ugandan succession fever
stories.summary: Image source, Uganda People's Defence Force (UPDF) Image caption, Gen Muhoozi Kainerugaba has signalled his intention to run for president in the next elections By Wycliffe Muia Published 14 November 2026 In Uganda's military, even senior generals are finding that their rank offers little protection from the wrath of the country's powerful army chief. Over the past 15 months, at least a dozen generals and senior officers have been arrested under Gen Muhoozi Kainerugaba, who is also the son of President Yoweri Museveni, in a crackdown that has unsettled the military's top ranks. The arrests come amid growing political tensions over who will succeed Museveni, who has ruled Uganda for four decades. Gen Kainerugaba, 52, is widely seen as a potential successor, although his ambitions appear to be facing resistance within the ruling party. This week, he threatened Vice-President Jessica Alupo with dismissal and possible arrest, while suggesting he should take her position.

stories.title: JOJ de Dakar, clap de fin : succès pour une première en Afrique
stories.summary: Clap de fin aux Jeux olympiques de la Jeunesse Dakar 2026. Après deux semaines de compétition, cinq pays africains se sont classés dans le top 10 des médailles, à savoir l'Égypte, l'Éthiopie, le Sénégal, le Kenya et l'Afrique du Sud, une première dans l'histoire des jeux. stories.title: Burkina Faso : mandats d'arrêt contre des journalistes et activistes en exil pour faits de "terrorisme"

stories.title: African Miss Universe Contestants Struggle to Get U.S. Visas

stories.title: Au Cameroun, les parlementaires sous la pression de la société civile pour légiférer contre les féminicides
stories.summary: Le thème des violences contre les femmes s’est peu à peu imposé dans le débat public, où le terme de « féminicide » a fait son apparition. Avant la fin de la mandature des députés, le 20 décembre, un dispositif juridique spécifique pourrait voir le jour.

stories.summary: 🍚🍕 Thiéboudiène, pâtes, pizza… Qu’est-ce qu’il y avait au menu des athlètes pendant les JOJ Dakar 2026 ? On vous emmène au cœur des cuisines où plus de 2 700 athlètes ont ainsi fait le plein d’énergie grâce à une organisation culinaire qui tourne 24h/24 !

stories.title: Paul Barril, French ‘Supergendarme’ Turned Mercenary, Has Died

stories.summary: Image source, AFP via Getty Images Image caption, Pro-government forces marched into Tigray's capital less than two weeks after the war began By Michael Teferi ,Â BBC Africa Â and Â Yemane Nagish ,Â BBC Tigrinya Published 13 November 2026 Running a hair salon in Mekelle, capital of Ethiopia's troubled northern Tigray region, is not easy at the moment. "People can't prioritise beauty over daily basic needs. For many residents, thinking about self-care is a luxury, at a time when they can't feed their kids," Firut Me'ar, who runs a salon in the city, tells the BBC. After a brief war, the city is under the control of the national army but life is far from normal, says Firut, a single mother of a 10-year-old daughter. "Things are better than during the war, but people still have no money, no morale. Business is almost non-existent," she says, her voice shaking with emotion. Above all, she says people are worried about what the future holds. "There is uncertainty about what comes next." Fighting broke out in late September between the Tigray People's Liberation Front (TPLF), the party that had run Tigray for decades, and the national army - a resumption of the two-year civil war that officially ended in 2022.

stories.title: Zimbabwean author Simbarashe Kundizeza cleared of using AI to write prize-winning story
stories.summary: ‘I am happy to put all this behind me and continue with my writing journey’ … Simbarashe Kundizeza View image in fullscreen ‘I am happy to put all this behind me and continue with my writing journey’ … Simbarashe Kundizeza Zimbabwean author Simbarashe Kundizeza cleared of using AI to write prize-winning story After a month-long investigation it was concluded that Kundizeza’s story The Blue Fighter, which won the £10,000 Caine prize, was ‘human-written’ The Zimbabwean author Simbarashe Kundizeza has been cleared of using AI to write a prize-winning short story, after the prestigious Caine prize for African writers concluded that his entry was “human-written” after a month-long investigation. Kundizeza’s story The Blue Fighter , which charts the declining fortunes of a family after the father invests in fish tanks, was announced as the winner of the £10,000 prize on 6 October. Five days later, the Atlantic published an article titled “Yet another literary prize winner seems to be AI”, in which the author and journalist Vauhini Vara said the AI-detection software Pangram, which itself uses AI, had deemed the story to be almost completely artificially generated. The Caine prize chair, Ellah Wakatama, said in a statement : “From our detailed investigation, we feel the evidence is clear: The Blue Fighter was human-written. We now look forward to awarding and celebrating Simbarashe Steyn Kundizeza … before the end of the year.” She said: “When concerns were raised, we have a duty as an organisation to look at them carefully and fairly,” adding that the prize had taken a “human-centred” approach to its investigation. “Our review included interviews with the author, the 2026 judging panel and The Shallow Tales Review, where the story was first published,” Wakatama said. “It also included independent and expert-led metadata analysis of drafts written by the author.” Kundizeza, who had strongly denied using generative AI to write the story, said he was “relieved” that the allegations had been dismissed after the investigation. “It was not necessary in the first place, I am happy to put all this behind me and continue with my writing journey,” he said.

stories.title: Kenya Starts Countdown to End of Ebola Outbreak
stories.summary: Advertisement SKIP ADVERTISEMENT Kenya began a countdown on Wednesday to declare the end of its Ebola outbreak. The final patient who had tested positive for the virus was discharged from the hospital on Wednesday. And the Kenyan cabinet secretary for health, Aden Duale, said at a news conference that the last 11 people being monitored for Ebola symptoms had also been discharged after completing a 21-day quarantine period. “For the first time since this outbreak began, Kenya has no patient under treatment and no contact in quarantine,” he said. The milestone is further evidence that countries have succeeded in containing the small number of cases, most coming in from the Democratic Republic of Congo, where the outbreak continues to spread. Since Kenya announced its first-ever Ebola case on Oct. 6, two people have died and nine have tested positive in the country.

Her tiny house lies just a couple of metres from the Ngong river, which runs through this densely populated area in the capital, Nairobi. The scars of floods in the long rainy season earlier this year can still be seen - including a broken TV in the corner which was immersed in water. Tucked out of sight is a photo of her sister Beatrice Khalayi, 58, who died when intense rains caused widespread destruction in Kibera. stories.title: Lewis Hamilton visits Egypt’s Rafah crossing and Gaza aid facilities
stories.summary: Lewis Hamilton with members of the Egyptian Red Crescent near the Rafah border crossing between Egypt and the Gaza Strip Photograph: Reuters View image in fullscreen Lewis Hamilton with members of the Egyptian Red Crescent near the Rafah border crossing between Egypt and the Gaza Strip Photograph: Reuters Lewis Hamilton visits Egypt’s Rafah crossing and Gaza aid facilities Seven-time F1 world champion tours border area and logistics warehouses operated by Egyptian Red Crescent Lewis Hamilton has visited Egypt’s Rafah border crossing with the Gaza Strip to meet organisations sending humanitarian aid to the territory. The seven-time Formula One world champion has spoken out about conflict and humanitarian crises in the region, and has called for peace. He has frequently posted on social media about children killed in Israeli airstrikes in Gaza and called for a ceasefire. “I think we need to make sure we’re pushing to free Congo, free Sudan, free Syria, free Palestine . I think there’s a lot of peace that I’m hoping we get to at some stage,” Hamilton said in October. A ceasefire agreement reached last year has halted major combat operations in Gaza, but the amount of aid reaching the territory continues to fall far short of the agreed-upon minimum of 600 trucks a day.
